tagline: A small town by the lake where you slow down and watch the sunset every evening
introHtml: Phayao is a quiet northern town built around Kwan Phayao, a wide freshwater lake right in the middle of the city. In the evening people gather along the water to sit, cycle, and wait for the sun to drop behind the hills. Around town there are old temples, mountains you can climb for a sea of morning mist, and small cafes that keep popping up one by one. If you like places that are in no hurry and easy to settle into, Phayao fits.
bestTime: November–February, cool and clear — comfortable for sitting by the lake

highlights.name: Kwan Phayao
highlights.blurb: The freshwater lake in the heart of town that defines Phayao. Every evening you can sit by the water and watch the sun set behind the hills.

highlights.name: Wat Tilok Aram
highlights.blurb: A temple in the middle of Kwan Phayao. Take a boat out to pay respects at the shrine in the lake — a must-stop for anyone visiting Phayao.

highlights.name: Wat Sri Khom Kham
highlights.blurb: The town's principal temple, home to Phra Chao Ton Luang, the largest Buddha image in the city, sitting right by the lake.

highlights.name: Doi Phu Langka
highlights.blurb: A well-known mist viewpoint in Pong district. Hike up and camp overnight to catch the fog in the morning.

highlights.name: Phu Sang & Chiang Kham district
highlights.blurb: The eastern side of the province has waterfalls, a national park, and Tai Lue culture for a taste of local life.

highlights.name: Phayao Walking Street
highlights.blurb: Open on weekends along the lake, with local food, craft stalls, and an easygoing small-town feel.

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, and gaeng hang lay are everywhere in town, cooked the way northerners really make it.

foodScene.name: Freshwater fish from the lake
foodScene.note: Kwan Phayao is a source of freshwater fish — lakeside spots serve grilled fish, fried fish, and tom yum with fresh catch.

foodScene.name: Sai ua & crispy pork rind
foodScene.note: Classic northern souvenirs and side dishes. Eat them with sticky rice or take a pack home.

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen nam ngiao
foodScene.note: Rice noodles in nam ngiao are a regular breakfast for locals — a tomato-based broth with dried red kapok flowers.

foodScene.name: Tai Lue food
foodScene.note: Around Chiang Kham there are Tai Lue communities with their own local dishes and distinctive chili dips to try.

foodScene.name: Lakeside cafes
foodScene.note: Coffee shops with lake views keep opening up — a good spot to sip and watch the water for a while.

foodScene.name: Phayao morning market
foodScene.note: The fresh market in town has local vegetables, northern snacks, and traditional sweets to graze on.

attractions.name: Kwan Phayao
attractions.blurb: The freshwater lake in the center of town — a spot for sunsets and evening rides along the water.

attractions.name: Wat Tilok Aram
attractions.blurb: A temple in the middle of the lake. Take a boat out to pay respects on the water — an atmosphere you won't find elsewhere.

attractions.name: Wat Sri Khom Kham
attractions.blurb: The town's principal temple, enshrining Phra Chao Ton Luang, a large Buddha image right by Kwan Phayao.

attractions.name: Wat Analayo Thipayaram
attractions.blurb: A temple on Doi Busarakham with sweeping views down over Kwan Phayao and the town.

attractions.name: Doi Phu Langka
attractions.blurb: The mist viewpoint of Pong district. Camp overnight to wait for the fog and the sunrise.

attractions.name: Phu Sang National Park
attractions.blurb: Home to a natural warm waterfall and green forest — good for hikers who want to wade in the water.

attractions.name: Wat Nantaram
attractions.blurb: A Shan-style teak-wood viharn in Chiang Kham, beautifully carved from old timber throughout.

attractions.name: Cultural Hall & Phayao old town
attractions.blurb: The old quarter by the lake where you can stroll, drop into a cafe, and learn about the town's history.

itineraryIdeas: Phayao 2D1N — the lake and temples in town
Phayao for nature — Doi Phu Langka and Phu Sang
